name: Transition Smoothness
description: Evaluates the degree of semantic overlap and lexical chaining between the end of one paragraph and the beginning of the next. Human writers naturally maintain thematic flow by referencing specific entities, concepts, or synonyms from the conclusion of a previous thought (the 'rheme') at the start of a new one (the 'theme'). Generative AI models, relying on broad contextual attention rather than human-like short-term memory continuity, often fail to create these tight lexical chains. Instead, AI compensates for poor semantic overlap by aggressively inserting generic transition adverbs (e.g., 'Moving forward', 'Additionally').
algorithm: Cross-Boundary Lexical Chaining & Semantic Overlap Analysis
mechanism: The algorithm isolates the 'tail' (last 1-2 sentences) of a paragraph and the 'head' (first 1-2 sentences) of the subsequent paragraph. It calculates the semantic overlap using vector embeddings and monitors for direct lexical chains (repetition of key nouns, pronouns, or direct synonyms). A text that consistently shows near-zero semantic overlap across paragraph boundaries, yet relies entirely on formal transition words to bridge the gap, is highly indicative of generative AI. High semantic overlap without the need for forced transitional phrases strongly suggests authentic human writing.
useCase: Best suited for analyzing multi-paragraph essays, articles, and reports where natural flow relies on building upon immediately preceding ideas rather than simply listing disjointed points.
strengths:
• Targets a specific cognitive limitation in how LLMs manage local attention boundaries versus how human working memory naturally bridges thoughts.
• Highly resilient against simple word-replacement strategies, as semantic overlap is an inherent structural property of the narrative flow.
limitations:
• Performance drops in highly structured, bulleted, or modular documents (like technical specifications) where paragraphs are intentionally siloed.
• May flag human writing that is poorly organized or overly reliant on disjointed 'topic sentences'.
parameters:
Analysis: Tail-to-Head Semantic Overlap
Metric: Density of Lexical Chains vs. Generic Adverbial Bridges
Output: 0-100 Transition Artificiality Score
accuracy: Moderate to High — 72-84% accuracy. It serves as a highly precise micro-structural metric that perfectly complements broader macro-level topic shift analyzers.

references.title: Hearst, M.A. (1997). TextTiling: Segmenting Text into Multi-paragraph Subtopic Passages. Computational Linguistics.
Crossley, S. A., et al. (2016). The tool for the automatic analysis of cohesion (TAACO). Behavior Research Methods.
